root_idea.summary: The root centers on motion as the opposite of stillness.
root_idea.development: The basic idea of motion extends to causing movement, agitation and activity, as well as to anatomical points associated with movement and implements used for stirring.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form II perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To move something; to set it in motion or agitation.
senses.usage_conditions: In the supplied Quranic occurrence, the object is the tongue in the construction لا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسَانَكَ, referring to bodily movement. The movement is understood as transfer or motion of a body, not as an independently abstract sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move or be in a state of motion, commotion, or agitation; to shake, wobble, wag, or nod; also to become active.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive use, contrasted with سَكَنَ ‘to be still’; the activity nuance is also used of lively growth or behavior.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike or injure the withers; in one reported construction, to cut or sever the neck with a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction involving the withers or neck.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be incapable of sexual intercourse; to be sexually impotent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical description of incapacity, with the related adjective also applied to a man and to a horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To urge a camel to go without succeeding in making it go.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized transitive use with a camel as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lively, active, agile, brisk, or sprightly; quick or sharp in intellect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective covering bodily liveliness and mental quickness; the cited application to a boy is illustrative rather than restrictive.
A noun opposed to stillness or lack of motion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The head or extremity of either hip or haunch that is next to the ground when sitting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical term; its plural forms refer to the corresponding hip extremities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Incapable of sexual intercourse; sexually impotent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use applied in the cited evidence to a man and to a horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weak in the waist or hip region, walking as though lifting the feet from the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical description associated with weakness of the حَرَاكِيك, the hip extremities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The withers or upper part of the withers of a horse, including the region where the shoulder blades meet and where the lowest part of the mane grows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may refer more specifically to the projecting bone or the place grasped by a rider.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The upper extremity of the neck at the joint with the head.
The mover or turner of hearts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional theological epithet applied to God in a traditional expression; it is not a separate Quranic occurrence in this packet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An implement for stirring a fire; also a style used to stir an ink receptacle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete instrument of stirring, with separate uses for fire and ink.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who keeps to or clings to the withers of his camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic description of a rider’s position on a camel.
